4|Abiraterone plus prednisone added to androgen deprivation
5|therapy and docetaxel in de novo metastatic castration-
6|sensitive prostate cancer (PEACE-1): a multicentre, open-
7|label, randomised, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design
8|Karim Fizazi, Stéphanie Foulon, Joan Carles, Guilhem Roubaud, Ray McDermott, Aude Fléchon, Bertrand Tombal, Stéphane Supiot,
9|Dominik Berthold, Philippe Ronchin, Gabriel Kacso, Gwenaëlle Gravis, Fabio Calabro, Jean-François Berdah, Ali Hasbini, Marlon Silva,
10|Antoine Thiery-Vuillemin, Igor Latorzeff, Loïc Mourey, Brigitte Laguerre, Sophie Abadie-Lacourtoisie, Etienne Martin, Claude El Kouri,
11|Anne Escande, Alvar Rosello, Nicolas Magne, Friederike Schlurmann, Frank Priou, Marie-Eve Chand-Fouche, Salvador Villà Freixa,
12|Muhammad Jamaluddin, Isabelle Rieger, Alberto Bossi, on behalf of the PEACE-1 investigators*
13|Summary
14|Background Current standard of care for metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer supplements androgen
15|deprivation therapy with either docetaxel, second-generation hormonal therapy, or radiotherapy. We aimed to
16|evaluate the efficacy and safety of abiraterone plus prednisone, with or without radiotherapy, in addition to
17|standard of care.
18|Methods We conducted an open-label, randomised, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design (PEACE-1) at
19|77 hospitals across Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and Switzerland. Eligible patients were male,
20|aged 18 years or older, with histologically confirmed or cytologically confirmed de novo metastatic prostate
21|adenocarcinoma, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1 (or 2 due to bone pain).
22|Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1:1) to standard of care (androgen deprivation therapy alone or with
23|intravenous docetaxel 75 mg/m2 once every 3 weeks), standard of care plus radiotherapy, standard of care plus
24|abiraterone (oral 1000 mg abiraterone once daily plus oral 5 mg prednisone twice daily), or standard of care plus
25|radiotherapy plus abiraterone. Neither the investigators nor the patients were masked to treatment allocation. The
26|coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival. Abiraterone efficacy was
27|first assessed in the overall population and then in the population who received androgen deprivation therapy
28|with docetaxel as standard of care (population of interest). This study is ongoing and is registered with
29|ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT01957436.
30|Findings Between Nov 27, 2013, and Dec 20, 2018, 1173 patients were enrolled (one patient subsequently withdrew
31|consent for analysis of his data) and assigned to receive standard of care (n=296), standard of care plus radiotherapy
32|(n=293), standard of care plus abiraterone (n=292), or standard of care plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone (n=291).
33|Median follow-up was 3·5 years (IQR 2·8-4·6) for radiographic progression-free survival and 4·4 years (3·5-5·4)
34|for overall survival. Adjusted Cox regression modelling revealed no interaction between abiraterone and
35|radiotherapy, enabling the pooled analysis of abiraterone efficacy. In the overall population, patients assigned to
36|receive abiraterone (n=583) had longer radiographic progression-free survival (hazard ratio [HR] 0·54, 99·9% CI
37|0·41-0·71; p<0·0001) and overall survival (0·82, 95·1% CI 0·69-0·98; p=0·030) than patients who did not receive
38|abiraterone (n=589). In the androgen deprivation therapy with docetaxel population (n=355 in both with
39|abiraterone and without abiraterone groups), the HRs were consistent (radiographic progression-free survival 0·50,
40|99·9% CI 0·34-0·71; p<0·0001; overall survival 0·75, 95·1% CI 0·59-0·95; p=0·017). In the androgen deprivation
41|therapy with docetaxel population, grade 3 or worse adverse events occurred in 217 (63%) of 347 patients who
42|received abiraterone and 181 (52%) of 350 who did not; hypertension had the largest difference in occurrence
43|(76 [22%] patients and 45 [13%], respectively). Addition of abiraterone to androgen deprivation therapy plus
44|docetaxel did not increase the rates of neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, fatigue, or neuropathy compared with
45|androgen deprivation therapy plus docetaxel alone.
46|Interpretation Combining androgen deprivation therapy, docetaxel, and abiraterone in de novo metastatic castration-
47|sensitive prostate cancer improved overall survival and radiographic progression-free survival with a modest increase
48|in toxicity, mostly hypertension. This triplet therapy could become a standard of care for these patients.

62|Introduction
63|After several decades with no substantial progress, the
64|treatment of de novo (synchronous) metastatic prostate
65|cancer has drastically evolved in the past 10 years
66|with the addition of diverse treatments to androgen
67|deprivation therapy (ADT), the former standard of care
68|(SOC). The prognosis for men with de novo metastatic
69|castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC) has been
70|improved by using ADT concomitantly with either
71|docetaxel1-5 or one of the second-generation androgen
72|receptor axis inhibitors (abiraterone,6-8 apalutamide,9 or
73|enzalutamide10,11). In 2018, radiotherapy to the primary
74|tumour was also shown to extend the overall survival of
75|patients with low-volume metastatic burden.12 The
76|benefits of these various combinatory therapies were
77|confirmed by meta-analyses13-15 and have helped to shape
78|the current guidelines for the treatment of mCSPC.16-18
79|Nevertheless, it remains to be established whether
80|merging some of these new therapies could provide
81|further clinical benefits and, if so, what combination
82|might be most suitable for de novo mCSPC.19 Conducted
83|by a European consortium (PEACE),20 this study aimed to
84|evaluate the efficacy and safety of abiraterone plus
85|prednisone, with or without radiotherapy, in addition to
86|SOC (ADT with or without docetaxel).
87|Methods
88|Study design and participants
89|We conducted an open-label, randomised, active-
90|controlled, phase 3 study with a 2 × 2 factorial design
91|(PEACE-1) at 77 sites across seven European countries
92|(Belgium, France, Ireland, Italy, Romania, Spain, and
93|Switzerland). The complete list of inclusion and exclusion
94|criteria is provided in the appendix (pp 5-6). Briefly, male
95|patients aged 18 years or older with histologically confirmed
96|or cytologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma
97|documented as de novo metastatic by bone scan, CT, or
98|MRI (according to Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid
99|Tumors [RECIST] version 1.1 criteria) and an Eastern
100|Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status
101|of 0-1 (or 2 due to bone pain) were eligible for inclusion,
102|provided they had received ADT for no more than
103|3 months before randomisation and had at least 6 weeks
104|between the initiation of ADT and the first docetaxel
105|dose. Patients with a pure small-cell carcinoma, or
106|previous prostate cancer treated by a definitive local
107|treatment were not eligible. All participants provided
108|written informed consent before any study-specific
109|procedures or randomisation were initiated.
110|The initial protocol was reviewed and first approved on
111|July 10, 2013, by the French Independent Ethics
112|Committee (Comité de Protection des Personnes Ile de
113|France VII). The protocol complied with the ethical
114|principles of the Declaration of Helsinki and was
115|approved by Institutional Review Boards at each study
116|site. The trial conformed with the International
117|Conference on Harmonization and Good Clinical
118|Practice guidelines, and applicable regulatory require
119|ments. Steering and Independent Data Monitoring
120|Committees roles and members are described in the
121|appendix (pp 3-4).
122|Two major protocol amendments were made during
123|the accrual period, to account for the evolution of SOC
124|for men with mCSPC. Although ADT alone was the SOC
125|when the trial began recruitment in 2013, the protocol
126|was amended on Oct 5, 2015 (273 patients had already
127|been accrued), to allow for docetaxel use in SOC
128|worldwide, after ADT with docetaxel had shown
129|improvement in overall survival.2,3 Then, in 2017, ADT
130|plus abiraterone was also shown to improve overall
131|Research in context
132|Evidence before this study
133|We searched PubMed from Jan 1, 1984, to Dec 31, 2012, for
134|papers in English, using the terms "prostate cancer",
135|"metastases", and "phase 3 trial", and found 16 studies. When
136|the PEACE-1 trial began in 2013, androgen deprivation
137|therapy (ADT) had for several decades been the standard of
138|care for men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate
139|cancer (mCSPC). All randomised trials conducted before the
140|mid-2010s had not shown improvement in outcomes with
141|new therapies compared with ADT. During recruitment for the
142|PEACE-1 trial (2013-18), overall survival of patients with de
143|novo mCSPC was shown to be improved by combining ADT
144|with either docetaxel or one of the second-generation
145|androgen receptor axis inhibitors (abiraterone, apalutamide,
146|or enzalutamide) and radiotherapy to the primary tumour, in
147|men with low metastatic burden. It had not yet been shown
148|whether combining some of these new therapies with ADT in
149|triple therapy could provide further clinical benefits.
150|Added value of this study
151|To our knowledge, PEACE-1 is the first trial to show that
152|a triple systemic therapy-consisting of ADT, docetaxel,
153|and a second-generation androgen signalling inhibitor
154|(abiraterone, combined with prednisone)-improves both
155|radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival in
156|patients with de novo mCSPC, without excessively increasing
157|toxicity (mostly hypertension and aminotransferase increase).
158|Implications of all the available evidence
159|The findings from the PEACE-1 trial, combined with the evidence
160|from other studies, add weight to the concept that systemic
161|treatment intensification provides clinical benefit for men with
162|mCSPC and illustrate that early treatment intensification is more
163|effective than identical or similar treatments being used
164|sequentially when the disease has become castration-resistant.
165|At a minimum, patients with mCSPC with a high metastatic
166|burden who are fit enough to be treated with docetaxel should
167|be considered for this triple systemic therapy.

4|survival compared with ADT alone.6,7 Thereby, an
5|additional amendment was filed on Aug 10, 2017, to make
6|docetaxel mandatory for the remainder of the patients to
7|be accrued, so that the trial could evaluate the addition of
8|abiraterone to ADT with docetaxel (given that the
9|evaluation of ADT plus abiraterone compared with ADT
10|alone had already been addressed by other trials). Further
11|details on the amendments to the protocol and statistical
12|analysis plan are provided in the appendix (pp 7-8).
13|Evolution of the sample size and allocation of patients
14|according to these key amendments is depicted in the
15|appendix (pp 9-10).
16|Randomisation and masking
17|Eligible patients were centrally randomly assigned in the
18|Alea Clinical Portal), in a 1:1:1:1 ratio, to SOC, SOC plus
19|radiotherapy, SOC plus abiraterone (abiraterone plus
20|prednisone), or SOC plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone.
21|This randomisation process was performed via the
22|Tenalea autonomous software, solely accessed by the trial
23|data manager within the Epidemioloy and Biostatistics
24|facility of the Gustave Roussy Center in Villejuif, France
25|until 2015, then by each investigator.
26|Randomisation was done using a minimisation
27|algorithm, stratified by study site, ECOG performance
28|status (0 vs 1-2), type of ADT (gonadotropin-releasing
29|hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy),
30|planned administration of docetaxel (yes vs no), and
31|disease extent or burden based on metastatic status
32|(lymph node metastases only vs bone metastases [with or
33|without lymph node metastases] vs visceral metastases).
34|A similar weight was given to each of the five
35|stratification factors, with 80% probability to minimise
36|imbalance in the number of patients assigned to each
37|treatment group. As the case report form gathered
38|information for patient stratification according to
39|high-volume versus low-volume metastatic burden
40|classification (as defined in the CHAARTED study2 [high
41|volume was defined as the presence of visceral
42|metastases or at least four bone lesions with one beyond
43|the vertebral bodies and pelvis]), this later classification
44|was retained to enable inter-trial comparisons. No
45|masking was performed in this study.
46|Procedures
47|In all patients in the study, ADT was planned to be
48|continuously maintained by either a gonadotropin-
49|releasing hormone agonist or antagonist, or bilateral
50|orchiectomy. Patients assigned to receive docetaxel as part
51|of SOC with continuous ADT were to receive six cycles of
52|intravenous docetaxel (75 mg/m2 per cycle; maximum
53|dose of 150 mg per cycle), to be administered every
54|3 weeks (plus or minus 3 days). Granulocyte colony-
55|stimulating factor (G-CSF) injections after each docetaxel
56|cycle were recommended until the protocol amendment
57|on Jan 22, 2018, made G-CSF prophylaxis mandatory for
58|patients who received docetaxel. The first docetaxel cycle
59|had to be administered within 14 days after randomisation
60|and be at least 6 weeks after ADT initiation. Patients
61|assigned to receive abiraterone received 1000 mg of
62|abiraterone (four 250 mg tablets, orally) once daily plus
63|prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily, starting within 6 weeks
64|after ADT initiation. PEACE-1 began accrual in 2013,
65|before the LATITUDE6 and the STAMPEDE7 abiraterone
66|trials were reported and before abiraterone was approved
67|for mCSPC, which is why we used 10 mg of prednisone,
68|similar to what is approved for metastatic castration-
69|resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Abiraterone and
70|prednisone (hereafter referred to as abiraterone) were
71|administered until disease progression to castration
72|resistance, withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity,
73|or death. Patients assigned to receive radiotherapy
74|(74 Gy in 37 fractions administered over 7-8 weeks)
75|were planned to start radiotherapy at least 3 weeks
76|after docetaxel completion (but no more than 8 weeks
77|after completion). Treatments given after disease
78|progression followed common practice, and investigators
79|were able to change therapy as they thought was most
80|appropriate, on the basis of prostate-specific antigen
81|(PSA) concentration variation or clinical progression,
82|even in absence of radiographical evidence. The treatment
83|flow chart is depicted in the appendix (p 10).
84|Every enrolled patient was to be followed-up for a
85|duration of 10 years. The complete list of assessments
86|performed at each visit and follow-up intervals are
87|detailed in the appendix (pp 12-13). Survival status data
88|were gathered within 3 months of the cutoff date for
89|97% of patients.
90|Outcomes
91|The coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-
92|free survival and overall survival. Radiographical pro
93|gression of soft-tissue lesions was evaluated by either CT
94|or MRI, on the basis of RECIST version 1.1. Progression
95|of bone lesions was assessed by bone scan according to
96|the adapted version of Prostate Cancer Working Group 2
97|criteria,21 with no secondary bone scan required to
98|confirm progression. Radiographic progression-free
99|survival was defined as the time between randomisation
100|and the occurrence of radiographical progression or
101|death from any cause. Overall survival was defined as the
102|time between randomisation and death from any cause.
103|Patients without events were censored at the date of last
104|follow-up.
105|The secondary endpoints were castration-resistant
106|prostate cancer (CRPC)-free survival, serious-genito
107|urinary-event-free survival, prostate-cancer-specific survival,
108|time to next skeletal-related event, PSA response rate,
109|prognostic study of serum PSA measured 6-8 months
110|after initiation of systemic therapy, time to pain pro
111|gression, time to chemotherapy for CRPC, quality of life,
112|changes in bone mineral density, correlation of biomarkers
113|with outcome, event rate per 100 person-years of treatment
114|analysis, and toxicity. CRPC-free survival was defined as

4|the time between randomisation and CRPC or death from
5|any cause. CRPC was defined as either radiographical
6|progression or a confirmed PSA rise (based on three
7|independent measurements: A, B, and C, with A<B<C,
8|and C≥0·50 ng/mL), with a serum testosterone within
9|castrated range (<0·50 ng/mL). Prostate-cancer-specific
10|survival was defined as the time from randomisation to the
11|occurrence of death from prostate cancer. The event rate
12|per 100 person-years of treatment was the number of
13|adverse events divided by the amount of person-time
14|observed (ie, 100 patients experiencing any adverse event
15|over a 1-year period of exposure, with an exposure time
16|from randomisation to CRPC or last follow-up). Adverse
17|events were graded on the basis of the National Cancer
18|Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse
19|Events version 4.0. Safety analysis was based on the highest
20|grade adverse event recorded during the period spanning
21|from treatment initiation to CRPC. Apart from CRPC-free
22|survival, prostate-cancer-specific survival, event rate per
23|100 person-years, and toxicity, secondary endpoint results
24|were still under investigation at the time this manuscript
25|was submitted and so are not reported here.
26|Statistical analysis
27|The initial protocol in 2013 planned for a sample size of
28|916 patients. However, due to a change in the SOC and the
29|knowledge gained from the LATITUDE and STAMPEDE
30|trial results published in late 2017, the planned sample
31|size was increased to 1173 and the coprimary study aims
32|were revised (appendix pp 7-8). Because PEACE-1 was the
33|only phase 3 trial to date that could determine abiraterone
34|efficacy in patients with mCSPC receiving ADT plus
35|docetaxel as SOC, the timing of the final analyses was
36|based on this population (population of interest). Sample
37|size calculation was performed with East software (Cytel;
38|Cambridge, MA, USA), on the basis of the assumption
39|that no significant interaction would take place between
40|radiotherapy and abiraterone, to allow for a 2 × 2 factorial
41|analysis of abiraterone efficacy. For abiraterone efficacy
42|evaluation, the predetermined acceptable probability of a
43|type I error was set at 0·05, divided between the two
44|coprimary endpoints (0·049 for overall survival and 0·001
45|for
46|radiographic
47|progression-free
48|survival).
49|We
50|hypothesised that adding abiraterone to ADT plus
51|docetaxel would improve overall survival by 30% over a
52|median of 53 months and progression-free survival by
53|40% over 30 months. Hence, with 355 patients assigned to
54|ADT with docetaxel plus abiraterone (with or without
55|radiotherapy) and 355 patients assigned to ADT with
56|docetaxel
57|without
58|abiraterone
59|(with
60|or
61|without
62|radiotherapy), 249 deaths would give an 80% power to
63|detect an overall survival hazard ratio (HR) of 0·70 at a
64|two-sided α level of 0·049. With the same group allocation,
65|262 radiographic progression events or deaths were
66|predicted to have an 80% power to detect a radiographic
67|progression-free survival HR of 0·60 at a two-sided α level
68|of 0·001.
69|This trial had a factorial design, based on the
70|assumption that there would be no interaction between
71|abiraterone and radiotherapy. Before analysing the
72|various outcomes, the presence of such an interaction
73|for both coprimary endpoints was tested by analyses of
74|maximum likelihood estimates using a Cox model
75|adjusted for stratification factors (ECOG performance
76|status [0 vs 1-2], ADT type [gonadotropin-releasing
77|hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy],
78|metastatic burden [low vs high; as defined in the
79|Randomisation and masking section],2 and docetaxel
80|[no docetaxel before amendment vs no docetaxel after
81|amendment vs with docetaxel after amendment]). In the
82|absence of a qualitative interaction (p>0·05) between
83|abiraterone and radiotherapy, the groups were to be
84|combined two by two on the basis of abiraterone
85|administration, regardless of radiotherapy, before se
86|quentially assessing abiraterone efficacy first in the
87|overall population and then in the ADT with docetaxel
88|population (assuming the significance level was reached
89|in first instance). As the preplanned number of pro
90|gression-free survival and overall survival events had
91|not been reached in the study population at the time
92|this paper was written, the efficacy of radiotherapy
93|remains to be analysed (appendix p 16). The coprimary
94|endpoint results presented here correspond to the final
95|planned analysis; no interim analysis was conducted.
96|All efficacy analyses were conducted in the intention-to-
97|treat population, defined as all patients who were
98|randomly assigned to a treatment group. Safety analyses
99|were conducted in the safety population, according to
100|the treatment actually received by the patients (those
101|who did not receive any investigational treatment were
102|not included in the safety analyses).
103|The median follow-up was estimated by the inverse
104|Kaplan-Meier method. Time-to-event endpoints were
105|estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method. The Cox
106|proportional hazards model adjusted for radiotherapy
107|and stratification factors provided significances and an
108|estimate of the abiraterone effect (p value and HR with
109|CIs adjusted to match adjustment made to significance
110|levels in the corresponding test [ie, 99·9% for
111|radiographic progression-free survival, 95·1% for overall
112|survival, and 95% for secondary endpoints]). The
113|assumption of proportional hazards was evaluated on
114|the basis of the weighted Schoenfeld residuals. The
115|heterogeneity of the effect of abiraterone in the
116|predefined stratification subgroups was evaluated using
117|Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for radio
118|therapy and stratification factors and including an
119|interaction term between abiraterone and the studied

4|Discussion
5|To our knowledge, this is the first trial to show that a
6|triple systemic therapy, consisting of ADT, docetaxel,
7|and a second-generation androgen signalling inhibitor
8|(abiraterone), extends radiographic progression-free survival
9|and overall survival in patients with de novo mCSPC.
10|Whether the systemic treatment of high-volume disease
11|(ie, extended metastatic spread) should differ from that of
12|low-volume disease has been extensively debated. The
13|benefit of ADT with docetaxel has been clearly shown for
14|patients with mCSPC with high-volume disease,4,22 but
15|data collected from larger populations support a similar
16|benefit across high-volume and low-volume disease.3 This
17|discrepancy might result from different ratios of patients
18|with de novo versus relapsing low-volume disease being
19|included in these trials, because recurrences favour better
20|prognoses.23 Second-generation androgen receptor axis
21|inhibitors have shown overall survival benefits in patients
22|with mCSPC regardless of the disease volume
23|considered.5,9,10 In this trial, the mature data for men with
24|high-volume disease indicate a clear improvement in
25|both radiographic progression-free survival and overall
26|survival when abiraterone is added to ADT with docetaxel.
27|Even though the data on overall survival were immature
28|for patients with low-volume disease, an abiraterone-
29|mediated benefit in radiographic progression-free
30|survival was already apparent. Thus, ADT with docetaxel
31|plus abiraterone should be proposed as a new SOC for
32|patients presenting with high-volume disease who are fit
33|for docetaxel prescription. However, for patients with low-
34|volume disease, the decision of whether to use two or
35|three agents should be carefully considered by both the
36|patients and their oncologists, to determine whether a
37|major benefit in radiographic progression-free survival
38|(HR 0·58) is sufficient to justify a treatment inten
39|sification in a context of immature overall survival data. It
40|would also depend on whether an overall survival benefit
41|is required. Long-term data and consensus conferences
42|will allow for clinical practice guidance refinement.
43|As abiraterone can inhibit CYP3A4 in vitro,24 and as
44|CYP3A4 is involved in docetaxel elimination,25 the
45|concomitant administration of these two drugs could
46|potentially increase docetaxel exposure and thereby its
47|toxicity. However, no increase in chemotherapy-related
48|side-effects occurred in reaction to this concomitance,
49|which might suggest an absence of substantial drug-
50|drug interactions between abiraterone and docetaxel.
51|This finding is consistent with the observation that
52|abiraterone and docetaxel have similar pharmacokinetic
53|behaviour when administered alone or in combination.26
54|Similarly, abiraterone did not affect the clearance of
55|another taxane, cabazitaxel, by CYP3A.27 We also did not
56|observe an increase in haematological toxicity when

In addition, they do not display absolute cross- 7|resistance, as abiraterone improves overall survival 8|after docetaxel treatment and docetaxel retains some 9|activity after abiraterone failure.30,31 Collectively, these 10|observations provide a rationale for the survival benefits 11|resulting from their combination in this trial. However, 12|this study did not answer whether this triple 13|combination yields clinical advantages over ADT plus a 14|second-generation androgen receptor axis inhibitor. 15|Indeed, at the time when this trial was conducted 16|(2013-18), combining ADT with such an inhibitor had 17|not been approved for mCSPC, thereby precluding 18|such a comparison within the trial. Incidentally, the 19|ongoing phase 3 ARASENS (NCT02799602) and 20|ENZAMET (NCT02446405) trials are also testing the 21|combined efficacy of second-generation androgen 22|receptor axis inhibitors (darolutamide and enzalutamide, 23|respectively) with ADT and docetaxel, and their 24|upcoming overall survival results will put the benefits 25|of abiraterone in perspective. 26|Reaching treatment synergy and preventing acquired 27|resistance despite tumour clonal heterogeneity are 28|cardinal aspects of mCSPC management that require 29|an optimisation of the treatment framework. In 30|PEACE-1, significant survival benefits were obtained 31|when abiraterone was added to ADT with docetaxel. 32|Remarkably, these benefits were observed even though 33|more than 80% of the SOC without abiraterone group 34|eventually received a second-generation androgen 35|receptor axis inhibitor (mostly abiraterone or enzaluta 36|mide) to address cancer progression. Indeed, by contrast 37|with previous trials, PEACE-1 investigators were allowed 38|to prescribe early salvage treatments to the control 39|group patients who showed evidence of cancer 40|progression. To this end, a PSA minimum value of just 41|0·50 ng/mL was used to define mCRPC, even in the 42|absence of radiographic progression. Collectively, these 43|observations suggest that the upfront combination 44|implemented in this trial is superior to the sequential 45|administration of these (or similar) agents as occurred 46|in the control group. Of note, abiraterone is approved 47|for metastatic prostate cancer in many countries and is 48|close to becoming a worldwide generic drug. 49|In conclusion, this trial not only confirms that 50|combining abiraterone with SOC improves outcomes in 51|men with de novo mCSPC, but it shows that combining 52|abiraterone with ADT and docetaxel improves overall 53|and radiographic progression-free survival and other 54|efficacy 55|endpoints 56|with 57|little 58|toxicity 59|increase. 60|Nonetheless, as PEACE-1 only included patients with 61|de novo mCSPC, it is still unclear whether this triple 62|therapy might benefit patients with metachronous 63|mCSPC. Our findings cannot directly address whether 64|this triplet systemic combination is superior to ADT 65|and abiraterone. Longer follow-up is required to answer 66|whether combining such an intensive first line systemic 67|treatment with radiotherapy to the primary tumour 68|might provide further clinical benefits for patients with 69|mCSPC. result.relation_rationale: The requested outcome is death from any cause measured from randomization in all randomized participants. The report defines overall survival the same way and censors patients without events at last follow-up. The analysis compares assignment to abiraterone versus no abiraterone, pooling radiotherapy assignments after finding no interaction; it reports the overall population, with 583 and 589 analyzed (one of 1173 randomized participants withdrew consent for analysis). questions.wording: Was the allocation sequence random?
questions.official_guidance: Answer ‘Yes’ if a random component was used in the sequence generation process. Examples include computer-generated random numbers; reference to a random number table; coin tossing; shuffling cards or envelopes; throwing dice; or drawing lots. Answer ‘No’ if no random element was used in generating the allocation sequence or the sequence is predictable. Answer ‘No information’ if the only information about randomization methods is a statement that the study is randomized.
questions.source_locator: Full guidance p. 17, Box 4, signalling question 1.1
questions.bias_construct: Whether a random component was used to generate the allocation sequence.
questions.decision_rule: Answer yes when a random component was used; answer no when no random element was used or the sequence is predictable. A statement that the study is randomized alone supports no_information.
evidence_needed: The sequence-generation method, such as computer random numbers, a random number table, coin tossing, or minimization with a random element.
questions.no_information_rule: Answer no_information when the only information about randomization methods is that the study is randomized. Do not turn missing reporting into proof that the sequence was non-random.

answer_anchors.text: A random component was used in sequence generation.
No random element was used, or the sequence was predictable.
The report only states that the study is randomized.

considerations: Minimization should generally be considered random when it includes a random element.

Sequence generation asks how the allocation sequence was produced; concealment asks whether forthcoming assignments were hidden before enrolment and assignment; baseline imbalance asks whether the resulting groups suggest a randomization problem. Evidence for one does not answer the others.
The baseline-imbalance answer must not change this answer.

response_framework.firm_evidence_rule: The definitive versions (‘Yes’ and ‘No’) would typically imply that firm evidence is available in relation to the signalling question.
response_framework.probable_judgment_rule: The ‘Probably’ versions would typically imply that a judgement has been made. ‘Yes’ and ‘Probably yes’ have the same implications for risk of bias, as do ‘No’ and ‘Probably no’.
response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.
response_framework.quotation_rule: Brief direct quotations from the text of the study report should be used whenever possible to support the answer.

additional amendment was filed on Aug 10, 2017, to make
docetaxel mandatory for the remainder of the patients to
be accrued, so that the trial could evaluate the addition of
abiraterone to ADT with docetaxel (given that the
evaluation of ADT plus abiraterone compared with ADT
alone had already been addressed by other trials). Further
details on the amendments to the protocol and statistical
analysis plan are provided in the appendix (pp 7-8).
Evolution of the sample size and allocation of patients
according to these key amendments is depicted in the
appendix (pp 9-10).
Randomisation and masking
Eligible patients were centrally randomly assigned in the
Alea Clinical Portal), in a 1:1:1:1 ratio, to SOC, SOC plus
radiotherapy, SOC plus abiraterone (abiraterone plus
prednisone), or SOC plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone.
This randomisation process was performed via the
Tenalea autonomous software, solely accessed by the trial
data manager within the Epidemioloy and Biostatistics
facility of the Gustave Roussy Center in Villejuif, France
until 2015, then by each investigator.
Randomisation was done using a minimisation
algorithm, stratified by study site, ECOG performance
status (0 vs 1-2), type of ADT (gonadotropin-releasing
hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy),
planned administration of docetaxel (yes vs no), and
disease extent or burden based on metastatic status
(lymph node metastases only vs bone metastases [with or
without lymph node metastases] vs visceral metastases).
A similar weight was given to each of the five
stratification factors, with 80% probability to minimise
imbalance in the number of patients assigned to each
treatment group. As the case report form gathered
information for patient stratification according to
high-volume versus low-volume metastatic burden
classification (as defined in the CHAARTED study2 [high
volume was defined as the presence of visceral
metastases or at least four bone lesions with one beyond
the vertebral bodies and pelvis]), this later classification
was retained to enable inter-trial comparisons. No
masking was performed in this study.
Procedures
In all patients in the study, ADT was planned to be
continuously maintained by either a gonadotropin-
releasing hormone agonist or antagonist, or bilateral
orchiectomy. Patients assigned to receive docetaxel as part
of SOC with continuous ADT were to receive six cycles of
intravenous docetaxel (75 mg/m2 per cycle; maximum
dose of 150 mg per cycle), to be administered every
3 weeks (plus or minus 3 days). Granulocyte colony-
stimulating factor (G-CSF) injections after each docetaxel
cycle were recommended until the protocol amendment
on Jan 22, 2018, made G-CSF prophylaxis mandatory for
patients who received docetaxel. The first docetaxel cycle
had to be administered within 14 days after randomisation
and be at least 6 weeks after ADT initiation. Patients
assigned to receive abiraterone received 1000 mg of
abiraterone (four 250 mg tablets, orally) once daily plus
prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily, starting within 6 weeks
after ADT initiation. PEACE-1 began accrual in 2013,
before the LATITUDE6 and the STAMPEDE7 abiraterone
trials were reported and before abiraterone was approved
for mCSPC, which is why we used 10 mg of prednisone,
similar to what is approved for metastatic castration-
resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Abiraterone and
prednisone (hereafter referred to as abiraterone) were
administered until disease progression to castration
resistance, withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity,
or death. Patients assigned to receive radiotherapy
(74 Gy in 37 fractions administered over 7-8 weeks)
were planned to start radiotherapy at least 3 weeks
after docetaxel completion (but no more than 8 weeks
after completion). Treatments given after disease
progression followed common practice, and investigators
were able to change therapy as they thought was most
appropriate, on the basis of prostate-specific antigen
(PSA) concentration variation or clinical progression,
even in absence of radiographical evidence. The treatment
flow chart is depicted in the appendix (p 10).
Every enrolled patient was to be followed-up for a
duration of 10 years. The complete list of assessments
performed at each visit and follow-up intervals are
detailed in the appendix (pp 12-13). Survival status data
were gathered within 3 months of the cutoff date for
97% of patients.
Outcomes
The coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-
free survival and overall survival. Radiographical pro
gression of soft-tissue lesions was evaluated by either CT
or MRI, on the basis of RECIST version 1.1. Progression
of bone lesions was assessed by bone scan according to
the adapted version of Prostate Cancer Working Group 2
criteria,21 with no secondary bone scan required to
confirm progression. Radiographic progression-free
survival was defined as the time between randomisation
and the occurrence of radiographical progression or
death from any cause. Overall survival was defined as the
time between randomisation and death from any cause.
Patients without events were censored at the date of last
follow-up.
The secondary endpoints were castration-resistant
prostate cancer (CRPC)-free survival, serious-genito

prognostic study of serum PSA measured 6-8 months
after initiation of systemic therapy, time to pain pro

8|The Independent Ethics Committee (CPP Ile de France VII, Hôpital de Bicêtre, 78, rue du Général Leclerc, 94270 Le

10|reviewed and approved the study documents, including the initial protocol, all subsequent amendments as well as all
11|information and documents provided to each and every patient included in this study. The initial protocol received a positive
12|review on July 10TH, 2013.
13|
14|An Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) and a Steering Committee were set up to ensure trial oversight,
15|enforce ethic, protect all patients, and evaluate benefit/risk ratios based on the independent review of all scientific results
16|during and after study completion. Steering Committee members are presented in section 3 below.
17|
18|Each and every eligible patient was informed about the risk and eventual benefit of the study they were about to join. They
19|were given enough time to understand the procedure, ask questions and consider their options before being required to sign
20|a dedicated informed consent form ahead of being centrally randomized.

24|Missing data

26|For rPFS and OS, missing values on the outcome were handled by means of censoring. Notably, recent vital status data
27|(obtained within 3 months of the cut-off date) were available for 97% of the study patients. All the efficacy analyses were
28|done on the 1172 patients from the ITT population, except the Cox model analysis used for the rPFS analysis (there were 6
29|patients with missing data for the stratification factor "Disease burden", hence discarded from the analysis). These 6 missing
30|data were recovered at time of OS analysis so that the Cox model applied to this analysis took into account the whole study
31|ITT population (n=1172).

4|Amendments to the study design and statistical analysis plan
5|Since PEACE 1 initial protocol authorization on July 13TH, 2013, the treatment of men with de novo metastatic prostate
6|cancer has drastically evolved. Consequently, the study design and statistical analysis plan had to be adapted accordingly.
7|Changes to the study protocol and statistical analysis plan were made without any reference to the outcomes data collected
8|during the study. All amendments to the protocol were validated by the Steering committee and the Independent Data
9|Monitoring Committee before being submitted to dedicated regulatory authorities (depending on the country in which is
10|located a specific participating site) ahead of implementation. Study amendments to the protocol that affected the course of
11|the study and/or impacted on the study analysis are presented in an itemized fashion below (numbering and date of approval
12|correspond to the one validated by the French regulatory authorities).
13|5.1
14|Initial version of the protocol
15|The initial version of the protocol aimed to include n=916 men with de novo mCSPC treated with ADT alone as SOC. With
16|458 allocated to ADT + abiraterone (arms B and D) and 458 allocated to ADT without abiraterone (arms A and C) and a
17|total number of deaths of 406, a 4% level two-sided test of equal exponential survival would have an 80% power to detect a
18|survival difference between abiraterone-treated and abiraterone-deprived arms with a constant hazard ratio of 0.75. With the
19|same number of patients, and total number of 627 CRPC events, a 1% level two-sided test of equal exponential CRPC PFS
20|would have an 84% power to detect an improvement in PFS with a hazard ratio of 0.75. The same hypotheses were made
21|regarding the OS and PFS improvement related to the addition of prostate radiotherapy to systemic treatment.
22|5.2
23|Study amendments
24|Amendment N°14 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 07-OCT-2015)
25|Several studies1-3 published after the initial approval of PEACE-1 protocol, established the benefit of supplementing
26|androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with docetaxel for diverse population of patients including de novo mCSPC patients,
27|the ones enrolled in PEACE-1. Therefore, the study protocol was amended to authorize the use of docetaxel as part of the
28|SOC, in patients fit to receive this treatment. Such a treatment came in effect in October 2015 at a time when 273 patients
29|had already been included. For patients unfit to receive docetaxel, the SOC remained ADT alone. The stratification factor
30|"docetaxel" (yes vs. no) was added to the randomization process. To adjust for the longer median overall survival mediated
31|by the addition of docetaxel, the median time expected in the control arm was increased by 1 year, to 5 years, and the
32|estimated follow-up duration after last patient entry until data maturity by 1 year bringing the expected study duration to 3
33|years of recruitment and 6.5 years of follow-up. The target hazard ratio and number of events (deaths) remained unchanged.
34|The IDMC pointed out that the initial sample size planned (n=916) would be underpowered with the addition of a new
35|group of patients (the docetaxel-treated) and that possible statistical interactions between the trial different components may
36|reduce the power of the study on the overall population. The submission of a revised statistical plan/sample size was
37|advised.
38|
39|Amendment N°20 (substantial; ethics committee approval: 10-AUG-2017)
40|The sample size was increased to 1168 patients (+250 patients) based on simulations incorporating a statistical quantitative
41|interaction between abiraterone and docetaxel. The clinical hypothesis was that the efficacy of abiraterone could be weaker
42|in patients treated with ADT+docetaxel compared to ADT alone as SOC. Based on the LATITUDE4 and STAMPEDE5
43|trial results (presented at the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) meeting in June 2017) demonstrating that the
44|upfront combination of abiraterone with ADT increased the overall survival of men with de novo metastatic prostate cancer
45|(PEACE-1 study indication) compared to ADT alone, it was no longer possible for ethical reasons to allow these patients to
46|be allocated to ADT alone when randomized to the SOC arm. Therefore, the protocol was amended to selectively restrict
47|accrual to the patients which could be treated with ADT+docetaxel (866 patients were already included at this time).
48|

answers.justification: The report says allocation used a minimisation algorithm with an 80% probability of minimizing imbalance across five factors. The stated probability establishes a random component in sequence generation, so the sequence meets the question's random-component criterion.

The report describes central allocation through the Alea Clinical Portal using autonomous Tenalea software. Until 2015 access was limited to the trial data manager, then investigators accessed it. The software-mediated central process supports concealment up to assignment; the report does not say that investigators could see forthcoming allocations after the access change, so this is probable rather than definitive.
unknowns: After 2015, the report does not describe what investigators could see before the portal assigned a participant or whether access was restricted to the next assignment.

answers.justification: The baseline table reports similar overall comparison-group sizes (583 versus 589) and broadly similar distributions across the listed prognostic factors, including age, ECOG status, stage, PSA, and metastatic burden. I see no substantial baseline imbalance suggesting a randomization problem.

result.relation_rationale: The requested outcome is death from any cause measured from randomization in all randomized participants. The report defines overall survival the same way and censors patients without events at last follow-up. The analysis compares assignment to abiraterone versus no abiraterone, pooling radiotherapy assignments after finding no interaction; it reports the overall population, with 583 and 589 analyzed (one of 1173 randomized participants withdrew consent for analysis). Thus the event definition, time origin, comparison, and outcome match, while the analysis excludes one randomized participant.

measurement.method: Time from randomization to death from any cause; patients without events are censored at last follow-up.

time_point_or_window.description: From randomization through the June 1, 2021 overall-survival data cutoff (median follow-up 4.41 years in the overall population).

One of 1173 randomized patients withdrew consent for analysis and was excluded.

questions.wording: Were participants aware of their assigned intervention during the trial?
questions.official_guidance: If participants are aware of their assigned intervention it is more likely that health-related behaviours will differ between the intervention groups. Blinding participants, most commonly through use of a placebo or sham intervention, may prevent such differences. If participants experienced side effects or toxicities that they knew to be specific to one of the interventions, answer this question ‘Yes’ or ‘Probably yes’.
questions.source_locator: Full guidance p. 28, Box 6, signalling question 2.1
questions.bias_construct: Whether participants were aware of their assigned intervention during the trial.
questions.decision_rule: Answer yes or probably yes when participants knew their assignment, including when intervention-specific side effects or toxicities revealed it. Blinding participants, commonly with placebo or sham intervention, may prevent such differences.
evidence_needed: A direct report of participant blinding, open-label conduct, or participant knowledge during the trial.
questions.no_information_rule: Use no_information only after considering direct facts, indirect evidence, and trial circumstances; an absent explicit awareness statement alone is insufficient when those facts support a probable judgment.

answer_anchors.text: Participants were aware of their assigned intervention.
Participants were blinded to their assigned intervention.

considerations: Awareness is about knowledge of assignment, not whether participants completed or received treatment.

response_framework.firm_evidence_rule: The definitive versions (‘Yes’ and ‘No’) would typically imply that firm evidence is available in relation to the signalling question.
response_framework.probable_judgment_rule: The ‘Probably’ versions would typically imply that a judgement has been made. ‘Yes’ and ‘Probably yes’ have the same implications for risk of bias, as do ‘No’ and ‘Probably no’.
response_framework.no_information_rule: Use ‘No information’ only when both (i) insufficient details are reported to permit a response of ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’, and (ii) in the absence of these details it would be unreasonable to respond ‘Probably yes’ or ‘Probably no’ in the circumstances of the trial.
response_framework.independence_rule: Signalling questions should be answered independently: the answer to one question should not affect answers to other questions in the same or other domains other than through determining which subsequent questions are answered.
response_framework.quotation_rule: Brief direct quotations from the text of the study report should be used whenever possible to support the answer.

traps: A no-hit search describes one lexical query, not scientific absence.

A treatment assignment or visibly different intervention does not by itself prove that participants or personnel knew the assignment.
Different treatment or visit schedules do not by themselves prove that outcome measurement differed between groups.
Stratification does not prove allocation concealment.

sections.excerpt: This question addresses whether the number of participants who were analysed in the wrong intervention group, or excluded from the analysis, was sufficient that there could have been a substantial impact on the result. It is not possible to specify a precise rule: there may be potential for substantial impact even if fewer than 5% of participants were analysed in the wrong group or excluded, if the outcome is rare or if exclusions are strongly related to prognostic factors.

answer_anchors.text: Carers or intervention personnel were aware of assigned intervention.
Carers or intervention personnel were blinded to assigned intervention.

questions.bias_construct: Whether carers and people delivering interventions were aware of participants' assigned intervention.
considerations: Assess the people delivering interventions, not merely outcome assessors.
questions.decision_rule: Answer yes or probably yes when carers or intervention personnel knew assignment, including when participant side effects or toxicities revealed it. If randomized allocation was not concealed, awareness by carers and delivery personnel is likely.
evidence_needed: A direct report of blinding or awareness by carers and people delivering the intervention, plus the allocation process when it bears on their awareness.
questions.no_information_rule: Use no_information when awareness of carers or delivery personnel cannot be determined.
questions.official_guidance: If carers or people delivering the interventions are aware of the assigned intervention then its implementation, or administration of non-protocol interventions, may differ between the intervention groups. Blinding may prevent such differences. If randomized allocation was not concealed, then it is likely that carers and people delivering the interventions were aware of participants’ assigned intervention during the trial.
questions.source_locator: Full guidance p. 28, Box 6, signalling question 2.2
questions.wording: Were carers and people delivering the interventions aware of participants' assigned intervention during the trial?

answer_anchors.text: The trial context caused protocol-inconsistent deviations.
No protocol-inconsistent deviation arose because of the trial context.
Reported details and trial circumstances do not support a judgment about trial-context-caused deviations.

questions.bias_construct: Whether deviations inconsistent with protocol arose because of the trial context.
considerations: Side-effect-related compromised blinding counts only when resulting changes were protocol-inconsistent and context-caused.

Subsequent treatment, rescue treatment, or cross-over is not itself a deviation for the effect of assignment: establish both protocol inconsistency and a trial-context cause before answering affirmatively.

Neutral contrast: protocol-permitted rescue after progression is ordinary subsequent care; prohibited rescue encouraged by trial staff is a candidate trial-context deviation. Change only the protocol-consistency and cause premises before changing the reasoning.
questions.decision_rule: Answer yes or probably yes only after establishing both that the change was inconsistent with the protocol and that the trial context caused it; identify both premises in the justification. Answer no or probably no when no such deviation occurred, including ordinary non-adherence outside the trial context, protocol-consistent changes, and protocol-permitted subsequent care after progression.
evidence_needed: Evidence linking the deviation to recruitment, engagement, or trial personnel and showing it was inconsistent with the protocol.
invalid_shortcuts: unequal post-progression treatment without evidence that it was prohibited and trial-context-caused
a protocol deviation without its cause
discontinuation or crossover without protocol and cause evidence
questions.no_information_rule: Use no_information when reported details are insufficient and trial circumstances do not support a reasonable probable judgment about trial-context-caused deviations.
questions.official_guidance: Answer ‘Yes’ or ‘Probably yes’ only if there is evidence, or strong reason to believe, that the trial context led to failure to implement the protocol interventions or to implementation of interventions not allowed by the protocol. Answer ‘No’ or ‘Probably no’ if there were changes from assigned intervention that are inconsistent with the trial protocol, such as non-adherence to intervention, but these are consistent with what could occur outside the trial context. The answer ‘No information’ may be appropriate.
questions.source_locator: Full guidance p. 28, Box 6, signalling question 2.3
questions.wording: If Y/PY/NI to 2.1 or 2.2: Were there deviations from the intended intervention that arose because of the trial context?

answer_anchors.text: The identified deviations were likely to affect the outcome.
The identified deviations were not likely to affect the outcome.

questions.bias_construct: Whether context-caused protocol-inconsistent deviations were likely to affect the outcome.
considerations: This question concerns the deviations already identified in 2.3, not any non-adherence in isolation.
questions.decision_rule: Answer yes or probably yes when the identified deviations were likely to affect the intervention effect estimate through this outcome; answer no or probably no when they were not likely to affect the outcome.
evidence_needed: A direct link between the identified context-caused deviation and this outcome or its effect estimate.
questions.no_information_rule: Use no_information when the effect of the identified deviations on the outcome cannot be determined.
questions.official_guidance: Changes from assigned intervention that are inconsistent with the trial protocol and arose because of the trial context will impact on the intervention effect estimate if they affect the outcome, but not otherwise.
questions.source_locator: Full guidance p. 28, Box 6, signalling question 2.4
questions.wording: If Y/PY to 2.3: Were these deviations likely to have affected the outcome?

answer_anchors.text: The identified deviations were balanced between intervention groups.
The identified deviations were not balanced between intervention groups.

questions.bias_construct: Whether context-caused protocol-inconsistent deviations were balanced between intervention groups.
considerations: Balance refers to the deviations identified in 2.3 and their potential effect, not to baseline group sizes.
questions.decision_rule: Answer yes or probably yes when the identified deviations were balanced between groups; answer no or probably no when they were not balanced.
evidence_needed: Group-specific counts or descriptions of the identified deviations and their comparability between intervention groups.
questions.no_information_rule: Use no_information when balance of the identified deviations cannot be determined.
questions.official_guidance: Changes from assigned intervention that are inconsistent with the trial protocol and arose because of the trial context are more likely to impact on intervention effect estimate if they are not balanced between the intervention groups.
questions.source_locator: Full guidance p. 29, Box 6, signalling question 2.5
questions.wording: If Y/PY/NI to 2.4: Were these deviations from intended intervention balanced between groups?

answer_anchors.text: An ITT or appropriate modified ITT analysis estimated assignment effect.
A naive per-protocol, as-treated, or inappropriate post-randomization exclusion analysis was used.

questions.bias_construct: Whether an appropriate analysis estimated the effect of assignment to intervention. Compare randomized assignment with the actual analysis population, grouping, reassignment, and exclusions, including their reasons; an ITT, modified ITT, or as-treated label alone does not establish this.
considerations: The question is about effect of assignment, so grouping must follow randomized assignment.
Assess what the analysis actually did, not the label attached to it: ITT/mITT/as-treated terminology is a description to verify against assignment, grouping, and exclusions.

Never-treated participants are not automatically participants with no adverse event or unavailable outcome. Recover the documented eligibility, outcome availability, and exclusion reason before judging the approved assignment-effect estimand.
questions.decision_rule: Consider ITT and modified ITT excluding participants with missing outcome data appropriate. Consider naive per-protocol, as-treated, and post-randomization exclusion of eligible participants inappropriate; post-randomization exclusion of ineligible participants may be appropriate when eligibility could not have been influenced by assignment.
evidence_needed: The actual analysis population and grouping rule: who was assigned, who was analysed in each group, who was excluded or reassigned after randomization, and why.
invalid_shortcuts: an ITT label without its population
a per-protocol label without the analysis population
questions.no_information_rule: Use no_information only after considering direct facts, indirect evidence, and trial circumstances; an incomplete analysis description alone is insufficient when those facts support a probable judgment about appropriateness.
questions.official_guidance: Both intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses and modified intention-to-treat (mITT) analyses excluding participants with missing outcome data should be considered appropriate. Both naïve ‘per-protocol’ analyses and ‘as treated’ analyses should be considered inappropriate. Analyses excluding eligible trial participants post-randomization should also be considered inappropriate.
questions.source_locator: Full guidance p. 29, Box 6, signalling question 2.6
questions.wording: Was an appropriate analysis used to estimate the effect of assignment to intervention?

answer_anchors.text: The wrong-group analysis or exclusions could substantially affect the result.
The wrong-group analysis or exclusions could not substantially affect the result.

questions.bias_construct: Whether failure to analyse participants in their randomized group could substantially affect the result.
considerations: This is conditional on an inappropriate or uncertain analysis in 2.6.
Assess potential impact only after deciding whether 2.6 was appropriate; a small or balanced exclusion can have low impact without making an inappropriate analysis appropriate.
questions.decision_rule: Assess whether the number analysed in the wrong group or excluded was sufficient for substantial impact. There is no precise percentage rule: fewer than 5% may still matter for rare outcomes or exclusions strongly related to prognostic factors.
evidence_needed: Counts and reasons for participants analysed in the wrong group or excluded, outcome rarity, and prognostic relevance of exclusions.
invalid_shortcuts: a group label without exclusion counts
questions.no_information_rule: Use no_information when the potential magnitude of impact cannot be assessed.
questions.official_guidance: This question addresses whether the number of participants who were analysed in the wrong intervention group, or excluded from the analysis, was sufficient that there could have been a substantial impact on the result. It is not possible to specify a precise rule: there may be potential for substantial impact even if fewer than 5% of participants were analysed in the wrong group or excluded, if the outcome is rare or if exclusions are strongly related to prognostic factors.

The funders of the study had no role in study design,

Results
Between Nov 27, 2013, and Dec 20, 2018, 1173 patients
were enrolled (one patient subsequently withdrew
consent for analysis of his data) and assigned to receive
SOC (n=296), SOC plus radiotherapy (n=293), SOC plus
abiraterone (n=292), or SOC plus radiotherapy plus
abiraterone (n=291; figure 1). SOC was ADT alone in
462 patients and ADT with docetaxel in 710 patients
(table 1).
For radiographic progression-free survival and overall
survival, the median follow-up periods were longer in
the overall population (3·5 years [IQR 2·8-4·6] and
4·4 years [3·5-5·4], respectively) than in the ADT with
docetaxel population (3·0 years [2·1-3·8] and 3·8 years
[2·9-4·5], respectively). Regardless of the population and
survival outcome considered, the median follow-up
periods did not differ between the groups who did or did
not receive abiraterone. For the radiographic progression-
free survival analyses, the median follow-up periods
from randomisation to the cutoff date of Sept 1, 2020,
were 3·53 years for the overall population (3·52 years for
the SOC without abiraterone groups and 3·56 years for
the SOC plus abiraterone groups; log-rank p=0·86) and
2·99 years for the ADT with docetaxel population
(3·00 years and 2·97 years; log-rank p=0·93). For the
overall survival analyses, the median follow-up periods
from randomisation to the cutoff date of June 1, 2021,
were 4·41 years for the overall population (4·44 years for
the SOC without abiraterone groups and 4·39 years for
the SOC plus abiraterone groups; log-rank p=0·98) and
3·81 years for the ADT with docetaxel population
(3·75 years and 3·85 years; log-rank p=0·95).
In the overall population (n=1172), no interaction

or

after

survival compared with ADT alone.6,7 Thereby, an
additional amendment was filed on Aug 10, 2017, to make
docetaxel mandatory for the remainder of the patients to
be accrued, so that the trial could evaluate the addition of
abiraterone to ADT with docetaxel (given that the
evaluation of ADT plus abiraterone compared with ADT
alone had already been addressed by other trials). Further
details on the amendments to the protocol and statistical
analysis plan are provided in the appendix (pp 7-8).
Evolution of the sample size and allocation of patients
according to these key amendments is depicted in the
appendix (pp 9-10).
Randomisation and masking
Eligible patients were centrally randomly assigned in the
Alea Clinical Portal), in a 1:1:1:1 ratio, to SOC, SOC plus
radiotherapy, SOC plus abiraterone (abiraterone plus
prednisone), or SOC plus radiotherapy plus abiraterone.
This randomisation process was performed via the
Tenalea autonomous software, solely accessed by the trial
data manager within the Epidemioloy and Biostatistics
facility of the Gustave Roussy Center in Villejuif, France
until 2015, then by each investigator.
Randomisation was done using a minimisation
algorithm, stratified by study site, ECOG performance
status (0 vs 1-2), type of ADT (gonadotropin-releasing
hormone agonist vs antagonist vs bilateral orchiectomy),
planned administration of docetaxel (yes vs no), and
disease extent or burden based on metastatic status
(lymph node metastases only vs bone metastases [with or
without lymph node metastases] vs visceral metastases).
A similar weight was given to each of the five
stratification factors, with 80% probability to minimise
imbalance in the number of patients assigned to each
treatment group. As the case report form gathered
information for patient stratification according to
high-volume versus low-volume metastatic burden
classification (as defined in the CHAARTED study2 [high
volume was defined as the presence of visceral
metastases or at least four bone lesions with one beyond
the vertebral bodies and pelvis]), this later classification
was retained to enable inter-trial comparisons. No
masking was performed in this study.
Procedures
In all patients in the study, ADT was planned to be
continuously maintained by either a gonadotropin-
releasing hormone agonist or antagonist, or bilateral
orchiectomy. Patients assigned to receive docetaxel as part
of SOC with continuous ADT were to receive six cycles of
intravenous docetaxel (75 mg/m2 per cycle; maximum
dose of 150 mg per cycle), to be administered every
3 weeks (plus or minus 3 days). Granulocyte colony-
stimulating factor (G-CSF) injections after each docetaxel
cycle were recommended until the protocol amendment
on Jan 22, 2018, made G-CSF prophylaxis mandatory for
patients who received docetaxel. The first docetaxel cycle
had to be administered within 14 days after randomisation
and be at least 6 weeks after ADT initiation. Patients
assigned to receive abiraterone received 1000 mg of
abiraterone (four 250 mg tablets, orally) once daily plus
prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily, starting within 6 weeks
after ADT initiation. PEACE-1 began accrual in 2013,
before the LATITUDE6 and the STAMPEDE7 abiraterone
trials were reported and before abiraterone was approved
for mCSPC, which is why we used 10 mg of prednisone,
similar to what is approved for metastatic castration-
resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Abiraterone and
prednisone (hereafter referred to as abiraterone) were
administered until disease progression to castration
resistance, withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity,
or death. Patients assigned to receive radiotherapy
(74 Gy in 37 fractions administered over 7-8 weeks)
were planned to start radiotherapy at least 3 weeks
after docetaxel completion (but no more than 8 weeks
after completion). Treatments given after disease
progression followed common practice, and investigators
were able to change therapy as they thought was most
appropriate, on the basis of prostate-specific antigen
(PSA) concentration variation or clinical progression,
even in absence of radiographical evidence. The treatment
flow chart is depicted in the appendix (p 10).
Every enrolled patient was to be followed-up for a
duration of 10 years. The complete list of assessments
performed at each visit and follow-up intervals are
detailed in the appendix (pp 12-13). Survival status data
were gathered within 3 months of the cutoff date for
97% of patients.
Outcomes
The coprimary endpoints were radiographic progression-
free survival and overall survival. Radiographical pro
gression of soft-tissue lesions was evaluated by either CT
or MRI, on the basis of RECIST version 1.1. Progression
of bone lesions was assessed by bone scan according to
the adapted version of Prostate Cancer Working Group 2
criteria,21 with no secondary bone scan required to
confirm progression. Radiographic progression-free
survival was defined as the time between randomisation
and the occurrence of radiographical progression or
death from any cause. Overall survival was defined as the
time between randomisation and death from any cause.
Patients without events were censored at the date of last
follow-up.
The secondary endpoints were castration-resistant
prostate cancer (CRPC)-free survival, serious-genito
urinary-event-free survival, prostate-cancer-specific survival,
time to next skeletal-related event, PSA response rate,
prognostic study of serum PSA measured 6-8 months
after initiation of systemic therapy, time to pain pro
gression, time to chemotherapy for CRPC, quality of life,
changes in bone mineral density, correlation of biomarkers

item.aggregated_output:
`reported.endpoint.name` and a complete quantitative tuple. A multi-span table
instead needs a cited header and quantitative-row span; the endpoint must occur
in its cited title/definition or header, and each tuple value must occur in one
of the cited header, row, unit, or footnote spans. `Total`, `Overall`, or a
similar aggregate label is not an endpoint name. Follow the tuple rules in
[Specify the Result](result.md).
Repair unsupported leaves with exact Source wording and better Evidence; a
support defect does not make the Result unavailable.

## Ground a Domain answer

Attach each basis to the active question it informs:

- `direct_support`: the passage states the answer premise;
- `indirect_support`: the passage establishes it through an explicit link;
- `contradiction`: the passage conflicts with the premise;
- `context`: the passage fixes scope or meaning;
- `inference`: the passage supplies facts from which you draw a stated conclusion;
- `absence`: an untruncated scoped search found no hits;
- `limitation`: an explicit unresolved premise and stopping rationale, with an
  optional current-Trial search receipt when retrieval provenance is useful.

Non-absence Evidence relationships use a selected Evidence handle, except
`limitation`, which uses an unresolved premise and a stopping rationale. A
directly read passage does not require a search receipt. An
`absence` receipt must
report `truncated:false`, `total_matches:0`, and `condition:"no_hits"`. A
positive search may support a limitation after you inspect the
relevant material, but it cannot support absence.

A relationship label never expands what the passage says. Keep plans separate
from conduct, analysis populations from observed outcomes, endpoint definitions
from measurement properties, and absence of reporting from absence of bias.
Reuse Result Evidence only when its exact premise answers the Domain question.
State inferred conclusions in the answer's `justification`, with the source
facts and any unresolved link. The server checks Evidence identity and structure;
you judge whether those facts support the answer.

## Build a Domain answer

Read this section before the first `validate_domain_assessment` call. Submit
one object for each question on the dependency-closed active path. The object
needs `question_id`, the exact permitted `answer`, at least one `bases` item,
`justification`, `unknowns`, and `counterevidence` for an active question.
Use the question card's `options`; the example values are fictional.

```json
{
	"question_id": "sq:randomization:sequence",
	"answer": "yes",
	"bases": [
		{"kind": "direct_support", "evidence": "eh_0123456789abcdef"}
	],
	"justification": "The inspected passage states that a computer generated random allocations.",
	"unknowns": [],
	"counterevidence": []
}
```

Use a limitation basis separately when the source leaves a premise unresolved.

Use these exact shapes for the three basis forms:

```json
{"kind": "context", "evidence": "eh_0123456789abcdef"}
{"kind": "absence", "search_receipt": "sr_0123456789abcdef"}
{"kind": "limitation", "unresolved_premise": "The captured reports leave this premise unresolved.", "stopping_rationale": "Relevant retrieval was reviewed, but the premise remains unresolved.", "search_receipt": "sr_0123456789abcdef"}
{"kind": "limitation", "unresolved_premise": "The captured reports leave this premise unresolved.", "stopping_rationale": "The relevant section was read, but the premise remains unresolved."}
```

`context`, `direct_support`, `indirect_support`, `contradiction`, and
`inference` use a selected `evidence` handle. `absence` uses an untruncated
zero-hit `search_receipt`. `limitation` uses an explicit `unresolved_premise`
and `stopping_rationale`. Its current-Trial `search_receipt` is optional and
may be truncated. When present, copy the actual receipt returned for the
current Trial. A basis kind describes how the premise is used;
it does not add facts to the cited passage.

## Recover an unresolved premise

Use this gap-directed Reason–Act loop when inspected Evidence leaves a material
fact unresolved. Keep the loop in one working assessment across searches and
cursors.

1. Reason. Start from the approved Result and inspected main-report passages.
   Record the exact unresolved fact, the named method or section reference and
   concrete study wording that would distinguish the possible answers, what
   inspected Evidence leaves open, and the likely Source that could resolve it.
   Prefer wording from an inspected passage over a methodological label from
   the question card.
2. Act. Inspect the active comparison card's complete `passage_groups` inventory
   when one is returned. `passage_groups` navigate captured Sources; they do
   not contain every intake condition. For declared omissions or file-level
   intake conditions, inspect `get_status.data.conditions` or call
   `list_sources(trial_id)`. Use each group's `source_id`, `page_count`, and
   `logical_path` to navigate it. Source navigation identifies pages with no extracted text; those
   pages may contain visual or otherwise unextracted material. A supplement,
   `other` document, or combined
   protocol can contain the needed plan or participant-flow detail. A Source
   role is a routing hint, never evidence about its contents or applicability.
3. Search the likely Source with concrete study wording. Use a methodological
   label only to supplement that wording. Use a no-hit's exact mode and
   per-term counts to decide whether another explicit query or direct section
   read could resolve the premise. If a result is truncated and has a
   `next_cursor`, continue the same query first when deeper ranked passages
   could resolve the premise. Use the final untruncated receipt when recording
   `absence`; a limitation may keep a truncated receipt or omit it. Change the
   query only when its wording or the premise warrants a change. For a
   Source-scoped miss, inspect the navigation entries. Use
   the unresolved fact, Trial context, term feedback, and literal Source wording
   to choose whether another query or direct section read could resolve it. Read
   relevant returned pages. Continue navigation when the displayed entries do
   not identify a useful page or query. Navigation entries guide inspection;
   cite Evidence from the inspected passage. Do not treat a no-hit or an
   uninspected hit as scientific absence.
4. After each search or read, update the fact to exactly one state: supported,
   contradicted, or still unknown. A hit remains a candidate until you inspect
   the complete passage.
5. If the returned hits do not address the fact, inspect the relevant section
   of the likely Source, including its contents or front-matter pages when
   needed, before recording a limitation. Exhausted query results or ranking
   pages are not an inspected section. If that section does not resolve the
   fact, use another relevant search or read when it could narrow the unresolved
   premise. Do not run every query suggestion or read every appendix by default.
6. Investigate the upstream premise first. If it remains unknown, preserve that
   uncertainty and follow the question card's activation rules. Before
   `validate_domain_assessment` and `save_domain_judgment`, revisit every
   still-material unknown against the Source inventory. Record the relevant
   section inspected and the facts that remain unavailable. If a fact
   remains discoverable within captured Sources and bounded cursor or page
   windows, make the next relevant search or read. Otherwise record a concise
   limitation with an explicit stopping rationale and, when applicable, the
   current-Trial search receipt. Stop as soon as an inspected passage contains
   the complete premise and select its exact boundaries. The limitation
   documents the information reached, not absence of the fact.

An unreported result does not show that participant outcomes were unobserved.
Missing reporting alone does not establish differential measurement or result-based
selection. This loop separates four observations: a page was retrieved, a useful
candidate was surfaced, a complete source window was read, and the premise was
actually supported. Only the last two can ground a Domain answer.

The Domain context also reports source-specific retrieval coverage. A match in a
multi-Source search belongs only to the Source that returned it. A paginated
session remains `retrieval_incomplete` until a terminal receipt closes a gap-free
rank sequence; a completed no-hit Source is a retrieval observation, not a
scientific absence claim.

Completion: each Source-owned assessable Result leaf has exact support, and each
active Domain answer has a valid basis for its stated premise and uncertainty.

result.relation_rationale: The requested outcome is death from any cause measured from randomization in all randomized participants. The report defines overall survival the same way and censors patients without events at last follow-up. The analysis compares assignment to abiraterone versus no abiraterone, pooling radiotherapy assignments after finding no interaction; it reports the overall population, with 583 and 589 analyzed (one of 1173 randomized participants withdrew consent for analysis). Thus the event definition, time origin, comparison, and outcome match, while the analysis excludes one randomized participant.
